notes: Cheyenne City Council approved a two-year Flock contract in November 2024 (signed December 2024) for 23 cameras on major roads, paid for with American Rescue Plan Act funds. Two published figures differ slightly: the Wyoming Tribune Eagle reported $143,450 over two years; WyoFile later reported $146,300 over two years. The council must decide by February (2027) whether to renew.

sources.notes: Wyoming Tribune Eagle reporting: 23 cameras, two-year contract approved Nov 2024, signed Dec 2024, $143,450 over two years.
sources.title: Debate continues around Flock cameras at 23 Cheyenne intersections

sources.notes: WyoFile reporting: 23 cameras, $146,300 two-year contract paid with ARPA funds, 30-day retention, renewal decision due by February.
sources.title: Amid national backlash, Wyomingites fight Flock while police defend surveillance cameras

notes: Jackson Town Council voted 3-2 in 2023 to spend $184,800 to purchase and install 30 Flock cameras; later town reports describe about 28 cameras operating. The council has since renewed the agreement at a reported cost of nearly $90,000 annually. First Wyoming community to deploy Flock.

sources.notes: WyoFile reporting: 2023 3-2 council vote, $184,800 for 30 cameras, renewed at nearly $90,000 annually, ~28 cameras operating, 90-day data deletion policy.
sources.title: Amid national backlash, Wyomingites fight Flock while police defend surveillance cameras

notes: Town of Glenrock operates four stationary Flock cameras on the outskirts of town plus one in neighboring Rolling Hills. The town put the contract's automatic renewal on hold until October 16, 2026 while the town attorney seeks clearer contract language; cameras continue operating during the pause. Chief says Glenrock does not participate in Flock's national data-sharing network.

sources.notes: Laramie Boomerang reporting: renewal on hold until Oct. 16, cameras still operating, 4 cameras around Glenrock plus 1 in Rolling Hills, added during a budget session; Douglas PD item is Motorola (not Flock) and excluded.
sources.title: Douglas discusses implementing controversial license plate reader tech as Glenrock puts its Flock camera contract renewal on pause

notes: Flock Safety approached the Laramie County Sheriff's Office about deploying cameras throughout unincorporated Laramie County; Sheriff Brian Kozak declined, citing Fourth Amendment concerns, and stated he has no plan to deploy them in the future.

sources.notes: WyoFile reporting: Flock approached the agency, Sheriff Kozak declined and said no cameras were deployed in unincorporated Laramie County with no future plans.
sources.title: Amid national backlash, Wyomingites fight Flock while police defend surveillance cameras
